title: paged KV cache: block manager eviction and pinning heuristics
author: Jordan Kim
description: Motivation: reduce KV cache memory churn and tail latency caused by suboptimal block eviction patterns under continuous batching and long-lived contexts. This PR implements a new eviction/pinning heuristic and refactors the block allocator to support reuse and locality-aware pinning TTLs. Key changes: 1) extract a BlockAllocator trait and provide a fast freelist-backed allocator with fast-path reuse for recently-freed blocks, reducing allocation overhead under high churn; 2) add an adaptive pinning heuristic that pins blocks used by hot prefixes for configurable TTLs and decays pin priority based on access recency and batch-locality; 3) locality-aware eviction scoring combining reuse-likelihood, GPU memory locality, and estimated per-request reuse; 4) expose runtime flags for tuning pin TTL and eviction aggressiveness; 5) add end-to-end microbenchmarks and integration tests to validate correctness and perf; 6) add observability: per-block metrics (pin_count, last_access_ts, reuse_hits) and eviction histogram. Checklist: - [x] design doc (linked in ENG-7523) - [x] unit tests for allocator and eviction policy - [x] integration tests with continuous batching harness - [x] microbenchmarks and perf numbers - [x] docs/ops notes for tuning flags Summary of outcome: merged after review and CI. Benchmark highlights run on r5-gpu-c4: tail P99 latency improved 18% on long-context generation workloads, median latency improved 6%, and total memory allocations per second decreased ~42% under synthetic churn workload. This change is backwards-compatible by default; pinning TTL and eviction aggressiveness are tunable. See release notes below for operator guidance.

Defaults are conservative; operators can tune pin TTL and eviction aggressiveness via runtime flags. See docs/operations/kv_cache_tuning.md for guidance.
